text.p: The following is a direct contribution from commodity statistician F.O. Licht in Ratzeburg, Germany. Please address any queries to Helmut Ahlfeld on +00 49 4541 88920.

Robusta futures in London ended lower on long liquidation in a continuation of Thursday's downward reversal to a fresh rally the day before. March lost $32 to close at $1,500 per tonne, while May gave up $29 to close at 1,497 per tonne. In New York arabica futures ended mixed in choppy dealings. Speculative profit taking and steady pressure on the March/May switch drove the March contract down more than 3.00 cents/lb to a low of 137.00 cents/lb before the market bounced back. March closed 90 points lower at 139.40 cents/lb, while May added 45 points to close at 134.95 cents/lb. The outer months closed 0.20 to 1.05 cents/lb higher. Traders await the latest CFTC commitment of traders report, which most market participants expect to show an increase in speculative long positions. Traders said that although speculators have done some profit taking, they are still overextended. Roasters have a difficult time as already hefty differentials climbed this week. Although Colombian dock workers returned to work a week ago following a nine-day strike traders said coffee exports have been slow getting back to normal.

UNITED STATES - US certified coffee stocks fell by 543 bags to 21,051 bags (21,594 bags) on January 30. Stocks in New Orleans fell by 43 bags to 4,757 bags (4,800 bags), while stocks in Miami declined by 500 bags to 15,769 bags (16,269 bags). Stocks in New York and San Francisco remained unchanged.

COLOMBIA - Following the recent rise in world market prices Colombia raised its internal coffee price by 12 per cent on January 31. Finance Minister Jose Antonio Ocampo said the new price is 248,125 pesos per 125 kg load. The Coffee Growers Federation cut internal prices by 14,000 pesos per 125 kg load on December 5. The controversial move was aimed at reducing the deficit of the national coffee fund. Ocampo said the price hike would cost the coffee fund about 155 billion pesos in 1997.

NORWAY - Norway imported 719,900 bags of coffee in calendar year 1996, 9 per cent more than was imported the previous year. Main suppliers of green coffee in 1996 were Brazil (179,000 vs 249,600 bags) and Colombia (157,000 vs 143,500 bags). Purchases from India increased to 41,600 bags, up from 11,200 bags the previous year.

ROMANIA - Romania imported 408,000 bags of coffee in January/November 1996, 77 per cent more than was imported the same period in 1995. Total imports in calendar year 1995 dropped sharply by 39 per cent to 243,200 bags. The main suppliers of green coffee in January/November 1996 were Brazil (87,600 vs 96,900 bags) and Indonesia (177,200 vs 33,800 bags).
